causes.text: Reuters reported that Apple was moving forward with developing a passenger electric vehicle and planned to produce its own car by 2024 using a novel battery design that could dramatically reduce costs and improve range, according to people familiar with the matter.

source_info.title: Apple plans self-driving car with next-level battery technology

effects.text: Tesla's stock declined sharply as investors digested news that Apple intended to build its own electric car; following the Apple report, Tesla shares fell around 6.5% during their debut in the S&P 500.

source_info.title: Tesla slides as it joins the S&P 500 and falls further on news of Apple car plans

causal_reasoning_chain.description: On Dec. 21, 2020, Apple's self-driving car program made headlines when Reuters sources said the company planned to launch a passenger EV by 2024 with a breakthrough battery design. This was interpreted as a signal that a powerful new competitor might enter the EV market.

Investors reasoned that Apple's deep pockets and technological expertise could challenge incumbent EV makers such as Tesla. Expectations that Apple might siphon demand and talent away from Tesla increased competitive anxiety among market participants.

Following the Apple report, Tesla shares shed about 6.5 % during their first sessions as a member of the S&P 500 on Dec. 22, 2020, reflecting investors' reassessment of Tesla's future market share and profit potential.

rationale: The appearance of a well-funded technology giant planning its own electric vehicle threatened to erode Tesla's competitive edge, prompting investors to sell Tesla shares.
counterfactual_analysis: If Apple had not signaled its intent to build an electric car, investors would not have priced in the prospect of heightened competition, and Tesla's stock decline on its S&P 500 debut likely would have been smaller.

adversarial_confounders.text: Tesla's inclusion in the S&P 500 created index-related rebalancing flows that also affected the share price.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Large index funds buying and selling could have influenced Tesla's stock independently of Apple's announcement.

details.commentary: Apple's decision to develop its own electric car signaled that a deep pocketed technology giant planned to enter the EV market and compete directly with existing manufacturers. Investors feared that a future Apple branded vehicle would intensify rivalry for premium buyers and erode Tesla's long run pricing power, helping to trigger the sharp pullback in Tesla's shares.
